title: On-call handoff - Dylan Reyes (2026-03-03) - draft
content:
Shift summary (overnight -> morning)

- Window: 2026-03-02 22:00 -> 2026-03-03 07:30 PT (handoff at 07:30)
- Primary focus: stable traffic after the 02:30 model rollout; watch latency and model-fallback alerts.
- Alerts fired: two related alerts but auto-resolved:
  * high-request-latency: api-gateway p95 spiked to ~950ms at 02:35 for ~5m, alerted then recovered when traffic shifted to fallback model variant (gpt-small-quant-v2). Root cause likely transient host drain during rollout.
  * batch-queue-backpressure: RPS burst at 04:10 caused batching queue to back up but autoscaler kicked and cleared in ~4m.
- No P1 incidents. P2 candidate: intermittent 502s for embeddings route (see below).

Open items / ongoing work

1) Embeddings 502s (low volume, reproducible)
   - Started: 2026-03-01 18:00
   - Symptoms: embeddings endpoint returns 502 for some requests from eu-west-1 region; retries succeed. Error pattern shows connection reset from model-host.
   - Investigations done so far:
     * Checked model host logs (host-embed-09): intermittent OOMs around large-batch requests, but memory not fully exhausted (GC spikes).
     * Local repro with the same prompt and batch size succeeds 9/10; failure correlates with concurrent compaction job (GC + checkpoint).
   - Temporary mitigation: route eu-west-1 embeddings traffic to next-compatible pool (embed-pool-b) via traffic rule (done 2026-03-02 22:45).
   - Next steps: schedule a controlled repro with debug logging, add memory headroom to pool, and open follow-up with infra team (JIRA: INC-3247 / ENG-889).

2) Model rollout follow-up
   - Rollout of gpt-4e-approx-v1 occurred 02:30; rollout policy used traffic-shadow then 10/30/60 percent steps. Latency profile showed slight p95 increase for generation route (~60ms).
   - Action: add rollout observation note to rollout ticket and mark as stable if no regressions by EOD.

Quick status checks (what I ran this morning)

- kubectl -n prod get pods | grep api-gateway -> all replicas Ready (6/6)
- kubectl -n prod logs deployment/ri-model-router -c router --since=30m | grep "fallback" -> a few fallback triggers around 02:35 (expected)
- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}
" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -> 200 0.120 (spot check)
- grafana: dashboards checked: per-route latency, model-pool utilization, batch-queue depth (urls in linked artifacts)

Escalation contacts (quick list)

- Oncall SRE (primary): Maya Singh (pager)
- Infra lead: Aisha Rahman (Slack/phone)
- Model ops: Leo Garcia (for model host issues)
- Product security: Jamie Chen (for any suspicious auth/keys)

Temporary procedures / emergency steps (draft)

Note: these are quick, minimal actions to stabilize traffic while we investigate — treat as temporary until infra changes are applied.

- If embeddings 502s increase (>=5% failure over 10m):
  1) Re-route region traffic to backup embed pool: run infra-routing cli -> `infra route set --service embeddings --region eu-west-1 --pool embed-pool-b`
  2) Scale embed-pool-b by +30% capacity: `k scale deployment embed-pool-b --replicas=<current*1.3>` (use exact numbers from the dashboard)
  3) Enable debug-level logging on model hosts for 15m: `ssh host-embed-09 -- sudo systemctl set-env LOG_LEVEL=debug && sudo systemctl restart model-service`
  4) Notify infra lead and tag JIRA INC-3247 with logs

- If API gateway p95 >1s for >10m and error rate >1%:
  1) Roll back the latest model rollout to previous variant: use rollout UI or `infra rollout rollback --id <rollout-id>`
  2) If rollback not possible, enable global fallback policy (route to gpt-small-quant-v2) via traffic-router: `infra traffic promote --model gpt-small-quant-v2 --percentage 100`
  3) Open P1 if user-facing impact observed (confirm with product/CS)

Runbook TODOs (things to clean up and move into canonical SRE playbook)

- Add exact infra CLI commands and flags to canonical doc (current ones are quick shortcuts).
- Add per-pool memory headroom recommendations based on batch-size histograms.
- Add automated health-check that detects GC+checkpoint overlap and pauses compaction during peak traffic.
- Draft a postmortem template for transient rollout regressions even when auto-resolved.

Notes to self / loose thoughts

- The embeddings failure pattern still smells like compaction timing + large concurrent batches — need telemetry that correlates GC/heavy-IO on hosts with batch arrival timestamps.
- Consider adding small random jitter to compaction windows across hosts (avoids synchronized GC).
- Re-check autoscaler logs for the batch-queue-backpressure spike; maybe tweak scale-up threshold from 75% -> 65%.

Handoff items for next oncall (Maya)

- Follow up with infra on INC-3247 and confirm whether memory tuning was already deployed to embed-pool-b.
- Monitor embeddings errors for 24h with extra alert sensitivity (set transient window to 3m).
- Keep an eye on rollout ticket for gpt-4e-approx-v1 and mark stable if no regressions by EOD.
- If you get more 502s, follow temporary procedure above and escalate to Aisha.

Unresolved questions (flag for post-shift)

- Did the compaction job schedule change last week correlate with more GC spikes? (check infra changelog)
- Could a different allocator or quantization tweak reduce peak memory per-host? Need model-ops input.

Quick links / references (copied for convenience)

- Grafana per-route latency: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency
- Rollout ticket: GH/infra Rollouts #482 (linked above)
- JIRA: INC-3247 (embeddings 502s)

-- End of handoff --

(Keeping this as a draft — will tidy and move to shared SRE playbook once we confirm root cause and temp fixes. Feel free to ping me in #oncall if anything is unclear.)
